Sword Atlas

Katana

刀

Origin
Japan
Period
c. 1400 to 1876
Blade
70 cm
Weight
1.0 to 1.3 kg
Edge
Single
Grip
Two-handed

The katana grew out of the older tachi, which was worn edge-down from the belt. As fighting on foot became common in the Muromachi period, samurai began wearing the blade edge-up through the sash, which let them draw and cut in one motion.

Smiths coated the spine of the blade in clay before quenching, so the edge hardened more than the back. That difference gives the katana its gentle curve and the wavy line called the hamon.

In 1876 the Haitōrei edict banned carrying swords in public, ending the katana’s role as the everyday companion of the samurai.
